Wafer Map Defect Classification¶

Objective¶

The primary objective of this project is to develop an Automated Defect Classification system using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN). By automatically categorizing spatial defect patterns on wafer maps, the system aims to replace manual inspection, reduce human error, and accelerate the identification of process anomalies.

Business Value¶

In semiconductor manufacturing, wafer map patterns provide critical insights into the health of the fabrication process. Specific spatial patterns often correlate with distinct equipment or process failures:

  • Yield Ramp-Up: Rapid identification of defect clusters (e.g., Scratch, Edge-Ring) allows process engineers to perform Root Cause Analysis (RCA) faster.
  • Cost Reduction: Automating the classification process reduces the "man-to-machine" ratio and minimizes the risk of misclassification due to operator fatigue.
  • Process Monitoring: Detecting systematic patterns (vs. random defects) helps in pinpointing specific faulty process steps, such as etching uniformity issues or CMP handling errors.

Data¶

  • Dataset: WM811K Wafer Map.
  • Scale: Contains over 811,000 wafer maps, with naturally occurring class imbalance (a common challenge in manufacturing data).
  • Features: The data consists of 2D images where each pixel represents a die's status (0: Background, 1: Good Die, 2: Defective Die).
  • Defect Classes: 8 specific patterns (Center, Donut, Edge-Loc, Edge-Ring, Loc, Random, Scratch, Near-full) plus a 'None' class.

Workflow¶

  1. Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA): Analyze class distribution and visualize spatial patterns.
  2. Data Preprocessing: Resize wafer maps to a standardized dimension (64x64 / 96x96) and apply denoising techniques.
  3. Model Architecture: Design and train a CNN tailored for spatial pattern recognition.
  4. Error Analysis: Investigate confusion matrices and "Hot Spots" to understand model limitations.
  5. Optimization: Implement Data Augmentation to address class imbalance and improve model generalization.

# Since most of the data is in the range of 25*25 to 75*75, we will try to resize them to 64*64 using cv2
TARGET_SIZE_64 = (64, 64)

def resize_wafer_map(wafer_map, TARGET_SIZE):
    """
    Resizes a single wafer map to the target size using Cubic Interpolation.
    """
    # cv2.resize expects pixels to be float or uint8. We cast to float32.
    # The wafer map values are 0, 1, 2.
    # We use nearest neighbor interpolation to preserve the discrete class labels (0, 1, 2) 
    # and avoid introducing non-existent intermediate values.
    return cv2.resize(wafer_map.astype(np.float32), TARGET_SIZE, interpolation = cv2.INTER_NEAREST)

# Apply resizing to the entire column
df_defect["waferMapResized"] = df_defect["waferMap"].apply(resize_wafer_map, TARGET_SIZE = TARGET_SIZE_64)

# Verify the change (only check the shape of the first resized image for convenience)
print(f"Original shape: {df_defect['waferMap'].iloc[0].shape}")
print(f"Resized shape: {df_defect['waferMapResized'].iloc[0].shape}")

# Visualize the comparison (Before vs. After)
plt.figure(figsize = (10, 5))

# Original
plt.subplot(1, 2, 1)
plt.imshow(df_defect["waferMap"].iloc[0], cmap = "inferno")
plt.title(f"Original: {df_defect['waferMap'].iloc[0].shape}")

# Resized

plt.imshow(df_defect["waferMapResized"].iloc[0], cmap = "inferno")

# Now we will finish the data processing part 
# But first we clean the test train label
df_defect["trianTestLabel"] = df_defect["trianTestLabel"].apply(lambda x: x[0][0] if len(x) > 0 else 'none')

# Then split the data based on the pre-defined label
train_val_data = df_defect[df_defect["trianTestLabel"] == "Training"].copy()
test_data = df_defect[df_defect["trianTestLabel"] == "Test"].copy()

# --- X Data (Images) ---
# 1. Stacking: Transform series into Numpy array
X_train_val = np.stack(train_val_data["waferMapResized"])
X_test = np.stack(test_data["waferMapResized"])

# 2. One-Hot Encoding: Transform (N, 64, 64) -> (N, 64, 64, 3)
X_train_val = to_categorical(X_train_val, num_classes = 3)
X_test = to_categorical(X_test, num_classes = 3)

# 3. Check Shapes
print(f"X_train_val shape: {X_train_val.shape}")
print(f"X_test shape: {X_test.shape}")

# --- y Data (Labels) ---
# 1. Create dictionary: { "Center": 0, "Donut": 1, ... }
unique_defects = sorted(df_defect["failureType"].unique())
label_map = {label: i for i, label in enumerate(unique_defects)}

print("\nLabel Mapping (Category -> Index):")
print(label_map)

# 2. Integer Encoding: Mapping the labels to integers
y_train_val = train_val_data["failureType"].map(label_map).values
y_test = test_data["failureType"].map(label_map).values

# Class Weights Calculation which we will be using later
class_weights = class_weight.compute_class_weight(class_weight = "balanced",
                                                  classes = np.unique(y_train_val),
                                                  y = y_train_val)

class_weight_dict = dict(enumerate(class_weights))
print("Class Weights:", class_weight_dict)

# 3. One-Hot Encoding
y_train_val = to_categorical(y_train_val, num_classes = len(unique_defects))
y_test = to_categorical(y_test, num_classes = len(unique_defects))

print(f"\ny_train_val Shape: {y_train_val.shape}")
print(f"y_test shape: {y_test.shape}")
print(f"Example Label (Original): {train_val_data['failureType'].iloc[0]}")
print(f"Example Label (One-Hot): {y_train_val[0]}")

# Now we train-test split the data
# We choose test_size = 0.2
# Since the dataset is highly imbalanced, we use integer labels for stratification to guarantee 
# that rare classes are adequately represented in the validation set.
X_train, X_val, y_train, y_val = train_test_split(X_train_val, y_train_val, 
                                                  test_size = 0.2, 
                                                  random_state = 42,
                                                  stratify = np.argmax(y_train_val, axis = 1))

print(f"X_train shape: {X_train.shape}")
print(f"X_val shape: {X_val.shape}")

X_val shape: (3525, 64, 64, 3)
In [10]:
# Now we can initialize the model
model = Sequential()

# Add Convolutional Layers 
# Layer 1
model.add(Input(shape = (64, 64, 3)))
model.add(Conv2D(32, (3, 3), activation = "relu", padding = "same"))
model.add(MaxPooling2D((2, 2)))

# Layer 2
model.add(Conv2D(64, (3, 3), activation = "relu", padding = "same"))
model.add(MaxPooling2D((2, 2)))

# Layer 3
model.add(Conv2D(128, (3, 3), activation = "relu", padding = "same"))
model.add(MaxPooling2D((2, 2)))

# Add Flatten Layer (Transition from 2D to 1D)
model.add(Flatten())

# Add Dense Layers
model.add(Dense(128, activation = "relu"))
model.add(Dropout(0.5)) # Prevent overfitting by randomly turning off neurons

# Output Layer: 8 neurons for 8 classes, utilizing Softmax
model.add(Dense(8, activation = "softmax"))

# Compile the model
# Loss: Categorical crossentropy is basically mandatory for one-hot encoded targets
# Optimizer: adam is a great default choice
model.compile(optimizer = "adam",
              loss = "categorical_crossentropy",
              metrics = ["accuracy",
                         # Precision: Crucial for trusting the model's diagnosis.
                         metrics.Precision(name = "precision"), 
                         # Recall (Sensitivity): Critical for rare but severe defect types
                         metrics.Recall(name = "recall"),
                         # AUC: Assessing the model's ability to distinguish between defect types.
                         metrics.AUC(name = "auc")])

# Show the summary
model.summary()

y_true = np.argmax(y_test, axis = 1)

# Make sure the index is in order
target_names = [k for k, v in sorted(label_map.items(), key = lambda item: item[1])]

# Compute Confusion Matrix and set the diagonal to 0 for better visualization
cm = confusion_matrix(y_true, y_pred)
np.fill_diagonal(cm, 0)

# Plot Heatmap
plt.figure(figsize = (10, 8))

# annot = True: Show numbers in cells
# fmt = "d": Format as integers
sns.heatmap(cm, annot = True, fmt = "d", cmap = "Blues",
            xticklabels = target_names,
            yticklabels = target_names)

plt.ylabel("True Label (Real Answer)")
plt.xlabel("Predicted Label (Model Guess)")
plt.title("Confusion Matrix")
plt.show()

# Printing metrics report
print("\n--- Classification Report ---")
print(classification_report(y_true, y_pred, target_names = target_names))

Top 3 Hot Spots:¶

True: Loc > Prediction: Scratch¶

The misclassification of "Loc" as "Scratch"is likely due to the loss of spatial resolution in deeper layers. As the image passes through successive Max Pooling operations, disconnected pixels can be merged into continuous lines (scratches) in the lower-resolution feature maps.

True: Edge-Loc > Prediction: Scratch¶

Similar to the previous case, the down-sampling operations in Max Pooling layers may cause the loss of fine-grained spatial resolution, leading to the merging of disconnected pixels into continuous lines (scratches).

True: Loc > Prediction: Edge-Loc¶

The confusion between "Loc" and "Edge-Loc" suggests the model struggles with spatial boundaries. The down-sampling operations in Max Pooling layers may be causing a loss of fine-grained spatial resolution, leading the model to merge 'Local' defects with the wafer edge boundary.

# Now we can initialize the model again
model_96 = Sequential()

# Add Convolutional Layers 
# Layer 1
# We increase the kernel size from (3, 3) to (5, 5)
# A larger receptive field (5x5) helps the model see "disconnected dots" (Loc)
# instead of just "continuous lines" (Scratch), reducing the confusion between them.
model_96.add(Input(shape = (96, 96, 3)))
model_96.add(Conv2D(32, (5, 5), activation = "relu", padding = "same"))
model_96.add(MaxPooling2D((2, 2)))

# Layer 2
model_96.add(Conv2D(64, (3, 3), activation = "relu", padding = "same"))
model_96.add(MaxPooling2D((2, 2)))

# Layer 3
model_96.add(Conv2D(128, (3, 3), activation = "relu", padding = "same"))
model_96.add(MaxPooling2D((2, 2)))

# Adding new layer to avoid overfitting
model_96.add(Conv2D(256, (3, 3), activation = "relu", padding = "same"))
model_96.add(MaxPooling2D((2, 2)))

# Add Flatten Layer
model_96.add(Flatten())

# Add Dense Layers
model_96.add(Dense(128, activation = "relu"))
model_96.add(Dropout(0.5)) 

# Output Layer
model_96.add(Dense(8, activation = "softmax"))

# Compile the model
model_96.compile(optimizer = "adam",
                 loss = "categorical_crossentropy",
                 metrics = ["accuracy",
                         metrics.Precision(name = "precision"), 
                         metrics.Recall(name = "recall"),
                         metrics.AUC(name = "auc")])

# Show the summary
model_96.summary()

# To address the observed overfitting and class imbalance, we introduce Geometric Data Augmentation. 
# By applying random rotations, zoom and flips, we simulate the natural variations found in wafer positioning 
# and improve the model's robustness against invariant features.

# Define the rules
datagen = ImageDataGenerator(rotation_range = 15,
                             shear_range = 0.05,
                             zoom_range = 0.05,
                             horizontal_flip = True,
                             vertical_flip = True,
                             fill_mode = "constant",
                             cval = 0)

# And the model is currently "over-predicting" Scratch.
# We need to reduce the penalty for Scratch to stop it from guessing Scratch for everything.

# 1. Identify the index for 'Scratch'
scratch_index = label_map['Scratch']

# 2. Reduce the weight by 0.4 (It's probably OK)
class_weight_dict[scratch_index] = class_weight_dict[scratch_index] * 0.4

print("Process compeleted")

# Now we initialize the model again (even though they are the same)
model_aug = Sequential()

# Add Convolutional Layers 
# Layer 1
model_aug.add(Input(shape = (96, 96, 3)))
model_aug.add(Conv2D(32, (5, 5), activation = "relu", padding = "same"))
model_aug.add(MaxPooling2D((2, 2)))

# Layer 2
model_aug.add(Conv2D(64, (3, 3), activation = "relu", padding = "same"))
model_aug.add(MaxPooling2D((2, 2)))

# Layer 3
model_aug.add(Conv2D(128, (3, 3), activation = "relu", padding = "same"))
model_aug.add(MaxPooling2D((2, 2)))

# Layer 4
model_aug.add(Conv2D(256, (3, 3), activation = "relu", padding = "same"))
model_aug.add(MaxPooling2D((2, 2)))

# Add Flatten Layer
model_aug.add(Flatten())

# Add Dense Layers
model_aug.add(Dense(128, activation = "relu"))
model_aug.add(Dropout(0.5))

# Output Layer
model_aug.add(Dense(8, activation = "softmax"))

# Compile the model
model_aug.compile(optimizer = "adam",
                  loss = "categorical_crossentropy",
                  metrics = ["accuracy",
                             metrics.Precision(name = "precision"), 
                             metrics.Recall(name = "recall"),
                             metrics.AUC(name = "auc")])

# Show the summary
model_aug.summary()

print(classification_report(y_true, y_pred_aug, target_names = target_names))

Conclusion & Future Work¶

Conclusion¶

In this project, we successfully developed an end-to-end Automated Defect Classification pipeline for semiconductor wafer maps. By progressing from a baseline CNN (64x64) to a higher-resolution model (96x96), and finally integrating Geometric Data Augmentation, we achieved the following key results:

  • Improved Feature Extraction: Increasing the input resolution to 96x96 allowed the model to better distinguish fine-grained defect patterns, such as distinguishing "Scratch" from disconnected "Loc" defects.

  • Enhanced Generalization: The non-augmented model showed signs of overfitting (divergence between training and testing loss). The final model, trained with data augmentation, demonstrated superior robustness. The gap between training and testing accuracy narrowed, indicating that the model is well-equipped to handle the rotational and positional variances inherent in real-world fabrication data.

  • Business Impact: This solution provides a scalable proof-of-concept for replacing manual inspection, potentially reducing the feedback loop time for Excursion Detection in high-volume manufacturing.

Future Work¶

To further improve the model's performance and production readiness, the following strategies are recommended:

  1. Transfer Learning: Instead of training from scratch, leveraging pre-trained architectures like ResNet or VGG16 could help extract more complex features, especially for subtle defect classes like "Edge-Loc".

  2. Handling Class Imbalance: Although augmentation helped, the dataset remains imbalanced. Implementing Weighted Loss Functions or synthetic data generation (e.g., using GANs or Variational Autoencoders) could further improve the detection rate for minority classes.

  3. Real-time Inference: Optimizing the model using TensorRT or model quantization to ensure it meets the low-latency requirements of inline wafer inspection tools.

Appendix: Experiment on Model Complexity¶

We also attempted to further improve performance using Batch Normalization and deeper Dense layers. However, results showed severe overfitting (Training Acc > 99%, Test Acc 74%), indicating that the simpler architecture generalizes better on sparse wafer map data. We leave the cells in the file for reference.

# Initialize
model_pro = Sequential()

# We add Batch Normalization to stabilize training and amplify the subtle spatial signals 
# required to distinguish between location-dependent defects

# Layer 1
model_pro.add(Input(shape=(96, 96, 3)))
model_pro.add(Conv2D(32, (5, 5), padding = "same")) # Note: remove activation inside Conv2D
model_pro.add(BatchNormalization())                 # Upgrade: Add BN
model_pro.add(Activation("relu"))                   # Apply activation after BN
model_pro.add(MaxPooling2D((2, 2)))

# Layer 2
model_pro.add(Conv2D(64, (3, 3), padding = "same"))
model_pro.add(BatchNormalization())           
model_pro.add(Activation("relu"))
model_pro.add(MaxPooling2D((2, 2)))

# Layer 3
model_pro.add(Conv2D(128, (3, 3), padding = "same"))
model_pro.add(BatchNormalization())            
model_pro.add(Activation("relu"))
model_pro.add(MaxPooling2D((2, 2)))

# Layer 4
model_pro.add(Conv2D(256, (3, 3), padding = "same"))
model_pro.add(BatchNormalization())               
model_pro.add(Activation("relu"))
model_pro.add(MaxPooling2D((2, 2)))

# --- Classifier ---
model_pro.add(Flatten())

# Expanding the dense layer from 128 to 256 to extract more features

# Upgrade: Increase Dense capacity from 128 to 256
model_pro.add(Dense(256))
model_pro.add(BatchNormalization())             
model_pro.add(Activation("relu"))
model_pro.add(Dropout(0.5))

# Add Flatten Layer
model_pro.add(Dense(8, activation="softmax"))

# Compile the model
model_pro.compile(optimizer = "adam",
                  loss = "categorical_crossentropy",
                  metrics=["accuracy",
                           metrics.Precision(name = "precision"),
                           metrics.Recall(name = "recall"),
                           metrics.AUC(name = "auc")])

# Show the summary
model_pro.summary()

# Define LR Scheduler
# If val_loss doesn't improve for 3 epochs, reduce learning rate by half
# to make finer adjustments and converge to a higher accuracy.
lr_scheduler = ReduceLROnPlateau(monitor = "val_loss",
                                 factor = 0.5, 
                                 patience = 3, 
                                 min_lr = 1e-6, 
                                 verbose = 1)

history_pro = model_pro.fit(datagen.flow(X_train_96, y_train_96, batch_size = 64),
                            epochs = 35,  
                            validation_data = (X_val_96, y_val_96),
                            steps_per_epoch = math.ceil(len(X_train_96) / 64),
                            class_weight = class_weight_dict, 
                            callbacks = [lr_scheduler])

            yticklabels = target_names)

plt.xlabel("Predicted Label (Model Guess)")
plt.title("Confusion Matrix")

# Visualize the training history
plt.figure(figsize = (12, 4))

# Accuracy
plt.subplot(2, 2, 1)
plt.plot(history_pro.history["accuracy"], label = "Train Acc")
plt.plot(history_pro.history["val_accuracy"], label = "Val Acc")
plt.title("Accuracy: Final Version")
plt.xlabel("Epoch")
plt.ylabel("Accuracy")
plt.legend()

# Loss
plt.subplot(2, 2, 2)
plt.plot(history_pro.history["loss"], label = "Train Loss")
plt.plot(history_pro.history["val_loss"], label = "Val Loss")
plt.title("Loss: Final Version")
plt.xlabel("Epoch")
plt.ylabel("Loss")
plt.legend()

# AUC 
plt.subplot(2, 2, 3)
plt.plot(history_pro.history["auc"], label = "Train AUC")
plt.plot(history_pro.history["val_auc"], label = "Val AUC")
plt.title("AUC: Final Version")
plt.xlabel("Epoch")
plt.ylabel("AUC")
plt.legend()

# Recall & Precision 
plt.subplot(2, 2, 4)
plt.plot(history_pro.history["val_precision"], label = "Val Precision", linestyle = "-")
plt.plot(history_pro.history["val_recall"], label = "Val Recall", linestyle = "--")
plt.title("Validation Precision vs. Recall: Final Version")
plt.xlabel("Epoch")
plt.ylabel("Score")
plt.legend()

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
